populationSource: _inbox/2026-09-17_p326-setback-residual-composition_measurement.json (byCity, no_ruled_table_all40), as restated by the first lane's table and by this dispatch. Counts below are P-326's, restated, NOT re-measured by this lane.
THE RULE THIS TABLE EXISTS TO KEEP: A class is a claim about what a city's own law says. It is NOT inferred from a search summary, is NOT inferred from a parcel carrying a district code, and is NOT inferred from a planning commission, a comprehensive plan or a real-estate field.

unclassified is a legitimate value. 8 of the 19 cities below are unclassified and are named with what would settle each. A city wrongly classed (b) freezes a fabricated line onto real parcels; a city wrongly classed (a) or (c) freezes a refusal or an absence. All four outcomes are sticky, so no row below is inferred.

The asymmetry that shaped the (a)-vs-(b)/(c) calls: (a) and (b) are EXISTENCE claims provable from one instrument; (c) is an ABSENCE claim that also needs the read to be complete. So this lane never writes (c) from a code that merely omits a zoning chapter (a zoning ordinance is frequently uncodified in Texas), and it never writes (b) from a line that the same code subordinates to something else.

Every source cited below is the city's own site/PDF or a code host carrying that city's code. The first lane's wrong-namesake failure mode (mart/crawford/creedmoor) was re-checked city by city under the admissibility rule registered in CP1, and ONE new wrong-namesake was caught this lane (webberville: webbervillemi.com is Webberville, MICHIGAN).

classA_zoned_ordinance_read.evidence: The city's own Code of Ordinances (eCode360, includes legislation through Ord. No. 06092025-02 adopted 2025-06-09) has no zoning chapter, but its Subdivisions chapter states the districts and the zoning ordinance govern: 'On the basis of the district in which they lie and the use to which they are to be put, all lots inside the city limits must conform to the regulations of the zoning ordinance, including minimum area, width, and depth.' and 'Conflict with zoning.
